rt.RT_cover:
- Purpose: Case-identifying information only.
- Typical content: case title, case number, parties, attorneys, court name, department, hearing date, reporter name/address.
- MUST NOT include verbatim dialogue.
- If there is any spoken dialogue on the page, it is NOT RT_cover.
rt.RT_body:
- Purpose: Verbatim transcript of proceedings.
- Required cue: Spoken dialogue with speaker labels or Q/A format.
- Can include a case header at the top, but must include dialogue somewhere on the page.
rt.RT_index:
- Purpose: Index/list of topics, witness names, or sections with page numbers.
- Typical cues: columns with Page or dotted leaders (e.g., Opening statement ........ 12).
- No verbatim dialogue.
rt.RT_certificate:
- Purpose: Certificate or attestation about the transcript's accuracy or preparation.
- Typical cues: CERTIFICATE, I certify, I, [name], do hereby certify, reporter/clerk signature line, date, seal, or notary language.
- No verbatim dialogue.
rt.RT_other: Other reporter-transcript material distinct from case-identifying covers, dialogue, indexes, and certificates of transcript accuracy. Use only when the visible content best supports this description after comparing all categories.

ct.CT_report:
Authored narrative or evaluative report prepared for the court, including continuation pages.
Look for a report heading, preparer or agency attribution, dated sections, findings, assessment or recommendations.
Footer report labels or codes such as CFS 6.7 and DCFS 4216 are supporting clues, not required names.
Distinguish reports from clerk-prepared minute orders, preprinted court forms, motions, notices and raw records or exhibits.
A report need not have an approved output name. Page X of XX numbering alone does not make it a form or exclude a report.
ct.CT_form:
Preprinted form with a form ID and Judicial Council approval in the footer.
   Form ID must be JV-XXX, FL-XXX, or ICWA-XXX.
   These forms DO show Page X of XX.
ct.CT_minute_order:
Clerk-prepared summary of a hearing.
   Often labeled MINUTE ORDER.
   Look for: appearances list, orders issued, judge/bench officer, court reporter, department.
   No verbatim dialogue.
   Not prepared by an attorney.
   These DO show Page X of XX.
ct.CT_certificate: Certificate executed by the clerk authenticating transcripts or documents.
ct.CT_proof_of_service: Declaration showing a party was served (mail, personal, electronic).
ct.CT_motion: A party's motion asking the court to act; may include points and authorities.
ct.CT_cover: Cover page for the clerk's transcript or a section (case caption, title, etc.).
ct.CT_index: Index/table of contents listing documents and page numbers.
ct.CT_other: Anything else (medical records, drug tests, service logs, letters, exhibits, photos, text messages, emails, case plans, written court order, etc.).

first_pages.first_hearing:
- The court is calling the case name or docket number.
- Parties or attorneys announce their appearances.
- The hearing appears to be starting (opening statements/roll call).
first_pages.first_minute:
- The minute order begins here (e.g., heading/title at top, start of order items).
- You may see a page indicator like Page 1 of X.
first_pages.first_form:
- The form begins here (e.g., heading/title at top, fresh form layout, start of sections).
- You may see a page indicator like Page 1 of X.
first_pages.first_report:
Look for a prominent report heading with a fresh opening layout, identifying fields, a report/hearing date, preparer or agency attribution, or introductory sections.
A first-page indicator can support a start. Repeated headings or report names in headers/footers alone do not establish a new report; continuing text or later sections without a fresh opening are continuation pages. Do not require an approved report name or decide whether this report should be summarized.
